Sources

Standards and sources

Every claim in the academy traces to a source with a version and a review date. This is the register, including what is verified and what still needs rechecking.

Source register

Review date 2026-11-24. Verified means read in this review. Carried means kept from the research blueprint and rechecked before release.

SourceRoleVersion and statusNotes
GIAC AI Platform Security (GAIPS)
GIAC		Flagship external benchmark for AI platform security.Verified
General availability 28 July 2026; multiple choice plus CyberLive, proctored, open book; exam structure subject to change.		The affiliated SANS page lists 2 hours, 54 questions and a 65% pass mark and groups the objectives into 8 domains. GIAC says length and structure can change, so confirm before relying on any figure.
GIAC AI Penetration Tester (GAIPT)
GIAC		Offensive benchmark for Level 5.Verified
Seven published objectives; covers agents, orchestration and MCP servers.		Not in Blueprint v2. GIAC also lists GASAE (security automation) and GOAA (offensive AI analyst, 10 objectives).
OWASP AI Security Verification Standard (AISVS)
OWASP		Testable requirements; lab rubric source.Verified
Version 1.0, June 2026: 12 chapters and 3 appendices. Version 1.01 is in progress.		Licensed CC BY-SA 4.0: cite requirement identifiers and paraphrase; copying text brings share-alike duties. Sources disagree on the count (191 requirements across 12 chapters in OWASP-linked sources; some blogs say 514 across 14), so cite the version and the chapter list from the repository.
OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
OWASP		Threat taxonomy ASI01 to ASI10.Verified
2026 edition; ASI01 to ASI10. Introduces the principle of least agency.		Names confirmed from the OWASP GenAI Security Project announcement and press coverage on the review date. Read the primary document before quoting any risk description.
MITRE ATLAS
MITRE		Adversary techniques, mitigations and case studies for AI.Verified
Monthly releases (version format YYYY.MM). A third-party count lists v2026.10 as the 38th release, published 28 October 2026.		Counts of techniques and case studies differ between sources and change monthly, so cite a release, not a number. MITRE’s OpenClaw investigation (9 February 2026) found seven new techniques and is a worked case for the detection lab.
MITRE ATLAS OpenClaw investigation
MITRE		Worked case for detection and red-team labs.Verified
Published 9 February 2026; case studies AML.CS0048 to AML.CS0051.		Read the case studies on the ATLAS site before building the lab.
NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative
NIST CAISI		Direction of travel for agent identity, authorisation and security.Verified
Launched 17 February 2026; the page was last updated in August 2026.		A programme, not a finished standard. Teach it as the direction of work and monitor for deliverables.
ISO/IEC 17024:2026
ISO and IEC		Design benchmark for the Intellica certification scheme.Verified
Third edition, published March 2026; adds provisions on AI in certification processes.		Its contents list includes a clause on how a certification body relates to education and training. Read the full text before designing the separation of teaching and certification.
EU AI Act and the Digital Omnibus on AI
European Union		Governance and legal literacy at Level 6.Verified
Law-firm commentary reports Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 in force from 27 July 2026, with high-risk obligations for stand-alone systems from 2 December 2027 and for embedded systems from 2 August 2028.		Secondary source. Confirm every date against the Official Journal and the European Commission timeline before publishing teaching material.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 and Generative AI Profile (AI 600-1)
NIST		Risk governance functions.Verified
AI RMF 1.0 (AI 100-1) is current; AI 600-1 final since 26 July 2024. A revision is in progress with no public draft seen on the review date. NIST released a concept note for an AI RMF profile on trustworthy AI in critical infrastructure on 7 April 2026.		Do not use an "AI RMF 2.0" label: NIST has not named a successor. The framework is voluntary and there is no NIST certification of it.
NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF) and SP 800-218A
NIST		Secure development, including generative AI model development.Verified
SP 800-218 version 1.1 is final (February 2022). Revision 1 (SSDF 1.2) was released as a draft on 17 December 2025. SP 800-218A (generative AI and dual-use foundation model practices) is final.		Teach 218A for model pipelines and watch Revision 1 for the final text.

How we use sources

  • Teach the concept in our own words. Cite requirement identifiers, not protected text.
  • Pin the version and the review date wherever a figure or a date appears.
  • Where sources disagree, say so and follow the primary source.
  • Standards change quickly. A scheduled scan and a change trigger update affected lessons, and the lesson changelog records it.
  • Paid standards are taught as concepts without reproducing protected text.

Reviewed 2026-11-24. Intellica is independent of GIAC, ISC2, ISACA, CompTIA, CSA, IAPP, OWASP, MITRE and NIST. Mappings show how our lessons relate to published objectives. They are not an affiliation, an approval or a prediction of any exam result.
